HEADLINE.finding: 2 of 8 sampled dead(T1) nodes FAILED exact certification, and NOT for margin reasons: verify_case found real HOLES (full unit squares with exact mass < 1), i.e. the float row oracle had missed violated placements even though the A27 rule (added_rows==0, minmass>=1) was satisfied. After feeding the witness rows back, both LPs re-converged to tau = 10.000000 = budget (node 50: 46 holes, 9.000 -> 10.000; node 93: 31 holes, 9.000 -> 10.000). Those two nodes are therefore NOT established dead.
HEADLINE.caveat: The re-solve ran at the hardened eps_geo = 0.003 (rows are shrunk squares, so tau_0.003 >= tau_true); tau = budget at that margin does not PROVE the nodes are alive. What is established is (i) the original certificates are invalid (exact holes) and (ii) the certification pipeline cannot kill them at the lab-standard margin.
HEADLINE.implication: The 36 unsampled kill(LP) nodes inherit this measured ~25 percent failure rate. Only 6 level-1 nodes + the root are certified today; the headline kill count of 44 carries an expected ~11-node certification debt.
